A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BirdSet and retain the same core datasets and benchmark experiments. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures and equations, support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original model-training and evaluation results across BirdSet datasets and three training scenarios, including means and standard deviations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains those original benchmark results and adds class-level inference results for ConvNext and Perch on HSN and POW in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The model architectures, BCE objective, focal-event processing and augmentation procedures remain unchanged in Appendix C. Renaming dedicated training as dedicated fine-tuning does not establish a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Both versions use XCL/XCM, dedicated XC subsets, VOX and the same eight soundscape datasets, including POW for validation. The new HSN/POW analysis uses existing coverage. Broader dataset comparisons and proposed self-supervised or few-shot applications do not establish additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: EfficientNet, ConvNext, AST, EAT, W2V2 and Perch remain the evaluated models. Appendix D reuses ConvNext and Perch; BirdNET supplies the threshold convention but is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds evaluation at a global prediction threshold of 0.1, reporting class-wise TPR, FNR, TNR and FPR on HSN and POW. The core splits, budgets and metrics remain unchanged. Section 4.1 newly describes EAT as AudioSet-pretrained, conflicting with Table 8; an actual pretraining change or experimental rerun is not established.

E4.justification: New Figures 14–15 examine species-specific detection errors and no-call behavior for two models on two existing datasets. Figure 9 adds named species-frequency breakdowns. These extend diagnostic analysis, while the original validation-loss analysis remains unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 8 replaces Perch's unspecified seed entry with 1, adding seed information without establishing additional runs. The trained models' run-count declarations and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged, including the existing inconsistency between the main text and Table 11's LT seed count.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the main benchmark table, renumbered from Table 5 to Table 3, and Appendix C Tables 9–11 match. V4 adds dataset statistics and threshold-dependent error results; for example, Figure 14 reports HSN whcspa TPRs of 0.21 for ConvNext and 0.28 for Perch at threshold 0.1.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 retains the same cmAP, T1-Acc and AUROC equations. No theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation is added or removed; the expanded discussion of learning challenges is conceptual.

C1.justification: V3 centers its contributions on standardized avian PAM classification. V4 presents BirdSet as a multipurpose resource for broader audio classification and representation learning, newly foregrounding quantitative volume advantages over AudioSet and a wider range of potential evaluation uses in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 reinterprets DT results as limited transfer from general audio pretraining instead of less effective, more costly training from scratch. V4 removes speculation about unavailable Perch settings explaining retrieval performance and explicitly acknowledges missing recent audio transformers and insufficient investigation of pretraining in Section 5.

D1.justification: Table 8 fills previously unspecified Perch details, including one million training steps, Adam, 160 mel bands and 750,000 training samples. These document the retained comparator rather than establish new BirdSet training runs. Appendix A adds a leaderboard address, and the datasheet specifies the 2021 eBird taxonomy.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning within general audio classification, with extensive comparisons against AudioSet, FSD50K, ESC-50, BEANS and BIRB. New references address audio datasets and self-supervised learning, including BEATs and masked audio autoencoders, while Table 7 adds a broader dataset comparison.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list and much of the challenges and conclusion are extensively rewritten around broader audio classification. DT terminology changes, ethics and reproducibility statements appear in the main document, and the new inference appendix moves the existing datasheet from Appendix D to E.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the introductory workflow figure with a dataset-volume comparison, merges the literature tables, redraws and moves the geographical map into the main text, and removes the vocal-complexity illustration. It also expands the dataset overview table and adds the broader dataset table, species-frequency plots and inference heatmaps.

improvement.justification: The new class-level diagnostics expose missed detections hidden by aggregate scores, while fuller Perch documentation makes the retained benchmark easier to audit. These provide a limited overall gain. New inconsistencies weaken the revision: Section 4.1 contradicts Table 8 about EAT pretraining, and Table 7 lists 10,296 training classes versus 9,734 in Table 2. The broader framing and unchanged core results do not establish a major improvement.
